service.name: Last Consulate
service.serviceType: Instrumental downtempo music for cocktail hours, dinners and corporate receptions
service.description: Last Consulate, one musician on upright bass and guitar over downtempo electronics, playing original instrumental music with jazz improvisation at conversation volume for arrival, cocktails and dinner at corporate events, galas and private dinners across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor.

faqs.a: Original instrumental music: upright bass and guitar out front over downtempo electronics, with jazz improvisation on top. It sounds closer to an early-2000s downtempo record than to a jazz set, and it's booked through Signet Artists in Denver.
It plays arrival, cocktails and dinner at about the level of the conversation, so your guests talk across it the whole time, and the bass lines are improvised live on the night.

faqs.q: Does it play covers or take requests?
faqs.a: No. Everything is original and instrumental, with no singer, which is part of why a client dinner books it: there's nothing on the night for the host to manage.

One musician and one rig. It sets up in about 6 by 4 feet on one dedicated 20-amp circuit, takes 45 minutes to set up, and plays through its own small sound system or the venue's house system, whichever the space wants.

faqs.q: Can it carry a whole evening?
faqs.a: Arrival through dinner, yes. When the night wants a dance floor afterward, a band or the DJ takes over on the same contract and the same sound system, so Last Consulate is the first half of one booking.
